questions.q: Which specific section of Rule IV identifies the five primary classifications of building construction based on materials and fire resistance?
questions.n: Section 401 is the foundational section that lists and defines Type I through Type V construction.

questions.q: A building is described as being 'four-hour fire-resistive throughout' with structural elements made of steel, iron, concrete, or masonry. Which type is this?
questions.n: According to Section 401.5, Type V is the most fire-resistive category, requiring a four-hour rating throughout.

questions.q: According to Section 402, a building can only change to a different type of construction if it complies with the new requirements, UNLESS the Building Official finds the new construction is:
o: Less hazardous based on life and fire risk
questions.n: Section 402 allows an exception if the proposed change reduces the overall hazard and risk.

questions.q: In Type IV construction, what is the required fire-resistive rating for the 'Structural Frames' as specified in Section 403?
questions.n: Section 403.1.c explicitly states that structural frames of Type IV construction must have a two-hour rating.

questions.q: Which test is used to determine the flame-spread characteristics of interior wall and ceiling finishes under Section 403?
questions.n: Section 403.2 mentions the 'Tunnel Test' as the standard for determining flame-spread and smoke density.

questions.q: Under Section 403, materials required to be flame-spread proofed must have a flame-spread rating of ________ or less.
questions.n: Section 403.2.c mandates that flame-retardant materials must have a flame-spread of 50 or less.

questions.q: Which type of construction allows the use of wood structural elements but requires exterior walls to be of incombustible fire-resistive construction?
questions.n: Section 401.3 specifies Type III as masonry and wood where exterior walls must be incombustible.

questions.q: For interior bearing walls, what is the required fire-resistive rating for Type V construction?
questions.n: Section 403.1.b explicitly requires a three-hour rating for interior bearing walls in Type V construction.

questions.q: The flame-spread requirements for interior finishes do NOT apply to which of the following?
o: Frames and trim of doors and windows
questions.n: Section 403.2.b exempts door/window frames and trim from these specific flame-spread requirements.

questions.q: What is the common fire-resistive rating required for exterior doors and windows across ALL types of construction?
questions.n: Section 403.1.d mandates a one-hour fire-resistive rating for exterior doors and windows regardless of construction type.

questions.q: Which construction type is defined simply as being made of 'wood construction' without additional fire-resistance mandates for structural elements?
questions.n: Section 401.1 identifies Type I as basic wood construction where structural elements may be any permitted materials.

questions.q: What is the minimum fire-resistive rating required for exterior bearing walls in Type IV construction?
questions.n: Section 403.1.a specifies that exterior bearing walls for both Types IV and V must have a four-hour rating.

questions.q: Which section of Rule IV should you reference to find the standards for interior wall and ceiling finishes?
questions.n: Section 403.2 contains the specific technical requirements for interior finishes and flame-spread tests.

questions.q: Type II construction requires the building to be 'fire-resistive throughout' for at least how many hours?
questions.n: Section 401.2 states that Type II wood construction must be one-hour fire-resistive throughout.

questions.q: True or False: In Type III construction, structural elements can be any materials permitted by the Code as long as the building is one-hour fire-resistive throughout.
questions.n: Section 401.3 allows various materials for structural elements in Type III, provided they meet the one-hour requirement.

questions.q: According to Section 403, what is the maximum smoke density allowed for interior finishes compared to untreated wood?
questions.n: Section 403.2.a states smoke density shall not be greater than that obtained from burning untreated wood.

questions.q: Which of the following materials is NOT listed as a primary component for Type IV or Type V construction?
questions.n: Types IV and V require incombustible construction; untreated wood is not a primary structural material here.

questions.q: Under Section 403, what is the required fire-resistive rating for 'Interior Bearing Walls' in Types II, III, and IV?
questions.n: Section 403.1.b mandates a one-hour rating for interior bearing walls for these three types.

questions.q: Flame-spread requirements do NOT apply to materials that are less than ________ thick and cemented to walls.
questions.n: Section 403.2.b exempts materials less than 1.00 millimeter thick when cemented to surfaces.

questions.q: Which professional official has the power to approve a change in construction type if the new design is 'less hazardous'?
questions.n: Section 402 explicitly designates the Building Official as the authority to approve such changes.

questions.q: In Type II construction, what is the specific exception allowed for permanent non-bearing partitions within the framing assembly?
o: They must have a four-hour rating.
They may use fire-retardant treated wood.
They must be made of pure masonry.
questions.n: Section 401.2 allows fire-retardant treated wood in non-bearing partitions if they maintain one-hour resistivity.

questions.q: Which construction type is characterized by having exterior walls made of incombustible fire-resistive construction while the interior structural elements are masonry and wood?
questions.n: Section 401.3 defines Type III as masonry/wood construction with incombustible fire-resistive exterior walls.

questions.q: According to Section 403.1.b, what is the required fire-resistive rating for the 'roofs' of Type V construction?
questions.n: Section 403.1.b specifies that while bearing walls need 3 hours, roofs in Type V only require 1 hour.

questions.q: Type IV construction specifies that walls, ceilings, and permanent partitions must be incombustible, with an exception for certain non-bearing partitions. What is that exception?
o: They may use one-hour fire-retardant treated wood.
They must be made of steel.
questions.n: Section 401.4 allows one-hour fire-retardant treated wood within the framing assembly of non-bearing partitions.

questions.q: For Types II and III construction, what is the mandated fire-resistive rating for the 'Structural Frames'?
questions.n: Section 403.1.c lists one-hour fire-resistive rating for the structural frames of Types II and III.

questions.q: If a Building Official approves a change in construction type, what is the primary factor they must consider based on Section 402?
questions.n: Section 402 allows changes if the new construction is 'less hazardous, based on life and fire risk'.

questions.q: What is the fire-resistive requirement for 'Exterior Bearing Walls' specifically for Type V construction?
questions.n: Section 403.1.a mandates a four-hour fire-resistive rating for exterior bearing walls of Type V.

questions.q: Under Section 403, what is the maximum toxicity allowed for the products of combustion from interior finishes?
o: No more toxic than burning untreated wood.
questions.n: Section 403.2.a states that products of combustion shall be no more toxic than burning untreated wood.

questions.q: Which construction type specifically mentions 'steel, iron, concrete, or masonry' for walls, ceilings, and partitions, but doesn't reach the 'four-hour throughout' standard?
questions.n: Section 401.4 describes Type IV using these materials but with lower overall hour ratings than Type V.

questions.q: Standards for materials used in stairs, exits, and roofs are governed by the NBCP as well as which other specific code?
o: The Fire Code of the Philippines
The Civil Code of the Philippines
questions.n: Section 403.3 states that standards for these elements are governed by the Fire Code of the Philippines.
